page: Microsoft Azure D32lds_v7 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance belonging to the Dldsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_tile and AMX_int8) for accelerated matrix operations, and Intel Vector Neural Network Instructions (VNNI). This instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It also includes 1890 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not bundle any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU hardware.

In benchmark evaluations, the D32lds_v7 demonstrates strong performance in specific compute-heavy and compression tasks. Single-threaded gzip compression reaches a top-tier throughput of 35.44 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieves a strong result of 202.24 GB/sec. For lightweight machine learning workloads, the CPU's AMX and VNNI instructions enable top-tier text generation speeds of 346.08 tokens/sec on small 135M parameter models, alongside strong prompt processing speeds of 192.12 tokens/sec on medium 7B parameter models. However, its memory-constrained profile is reflected in average scores across general multi-core stress tests, Passmark database operations, and large-block memory bandwidth write speeds of 63.7 GB/sec.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the D32lds_v7 is defined by its high compute density relative to its memory allocation. By pairing a fast 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon processor with a lean 64.0 GB memory footprint, this instance minimizes memory overhead costs for workloads that are primarily CPU-bound. The inclusion of 1890 GB of local storage provides a substantial high-speed temporary workspace. This hardware profile is highly suited for compute-intensive tasks with moderate memory requirements, such as web serving, file compression and decompression pipelines, batch processing, and CPU-based machine learning inference on small-to-medium models.
